justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Consultation Orchestrator and WebRTC SFU Media Server support R-01, Prescription Coordinator with Interoperability Adapter covers R-02, AI Gateway handles R-03, and Consent & Policy Engine addresses R-04 per purpose.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance in challenging conditions is addressed via Edge Router & TLS Terminator supporting HTTP/3 (QUIC), Bandwidth Adapter dynamic bitrate adaptation, Firestore regional caching, and asynchronous processing using Google Cloud Pub/Sub.
justifications.compatibility: Interoperability Adapter explicitly provides US FHIR Translator Component and EU National Gateway Adapter Component for regional standards (R-08), while secure mTLS links integrate external pharmacy networks and the AI Symptom Checker Engine.
justifications.usability: Patient Portal serves both Patients and Licensed Clinicians using SPA Router & View Manager and Offline Storage Manager. However, having clinicians share a single patient-centric portal container rather than a dedicated clinical workspace slightly limits clinician-specific workflows.
justifications.reliability: Degraded operation below 300 kbit/s is managed by Bandwidth Adapter and Janus Gateway fallback. Offline Storage Manager caches data locally, while Prescription Status & Retry Queue Component uses Dead Letter Queues for fault-tolerant messaging.
justifications.security: Strict data residency and privacy (R-05, R-07) are enforced via Geo-fencing & Context Injector, Consent & Policy Engine (OPA), Jurisdictional Storage Router, regional Cloud KMS keys, and write-once compliance logging in Audit & Version Logger.
justifications.maintainability: The architecture exhibits modular decomposition into cohesive containers and components (e.g., Core Telehealth Service, AI Gateway, Interoperability Adapter), isolating policy enforcement, external integration, and audit logging into independently testable and maintainable services.
justifications.portability: The system runs containerized microservices on GKE matching the target GCP regions. However, deep structural reliance on proprietary GCP services like Firestore, Cloud Endpoints, and Cloud Pub/Sub moderately impedes multi-cloud portability or infrastructure replacement.

PERF-01.justification: The WebRTC SFU Media Server with LiveKit and Consultation Orchestrator coordinates scalable streams. However, specific cluster auto-scaling rules and load balancing for 5,000 concurrent video sessions across SFU nodes are not fully elaborated in the component models.
tradeoffs: Resource cost of over-provisioned SFU media servers versus join latency

PERF-02.justification: At approximately 14 requests per second, the load is modest. The AI Gateway incorporates throttling, fallback proxies, and asynchronous audit logging to easily satisfy the 3-second threshold for 95% of requests.
tradeoffs: Synchronous upstream AI latency versus strict response time budgets

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture explicitly includes a Bandwidth Adapter for dynamic bitrate scaling, HTTP/3 (QUIC) termination for unstable links, and IndexedDB with Firestore sync to prevent clinical note loss during degradation.
sensitivity_points: Adaptive bitrate thresholds for 200 kbit/s streams
tradeoffs: Video quality reduction versus maintaining continuous uninterrupted audio and session state

AVAIL-02.justification: The target cloud specifies only us-central1 with no secondary US region or cross-zone disaster recovery topology. Complete regional failure cannot restore US service within one hour without routing data to the EU, violating residency.
sensitivity_points: Regional failover without violating data residency
tradeoffs: Disaster recovery availability versus infrastructure cost of multi-region US deployments

MOD-01.justification: The Interoperability Adapter encapsulates regional prescription protocols within dedicated components. Adding a new EU national standard is confined to the EU National Gateway Adapter Component without impacting core telehealth services.
sensitivity_points: Isolation of national prescription gateway protocols
tradeoffs: Dedicated adapter components versus shared abstraction layer complexity

MOD-02.justification: The Audit & Version Logger captures model versions and metadata in write-once storage. While traceability is fully addressed, runtime model version switching and rollback mechanics rely on the external AI engine.
tradeoffs: External engine dependency for model rollbacks versus in-house model hosting

SEC-01.justification: The Open Policy Agent-backed Consent & Policy Engine validates access rights before granting cross-region access. The Geo-fencing & Context Injector and Jurisdictional Storage Router ensure strict enforcement and comprehensive audit logging.
tradeoffs: Strict zero-trust cross-region checks versus clinician emergency access speed

SEC-02.justification: Consent states are managed in Cloud SQL PostgreSQL with row-level security and evaluated in real-time by the Consent & Policy Engine. Revocation takes effect immediately, verified via the Audit & Compliance Reporting Service.
sensitivity_points: Propagation delay of policy cache invalidation
tradeoffs: Immediate synchronous consent revocation versus background asynchronous cache invalidation
